title: Invited paper - Connecting the D.O.T.S.: Design of fluidic circuit boards for multi-OoC platforms using CAD Tools for Standardization
problem: Connecting multiple Organ-on-Chip (OoC) platforms in a standardized way remains a significant challenge. Current approaches lack unified design standards and connector specifications, limiting the ability to integrate multiple OoC components into complex, integrated systems on a single microfluidic platform.
motivation: Microfluidic chips enable multiple biological and chemical processes on a single platform. The Translational Organ-on-Chip Platform aims to combine multiple OoC components into more complex, integrated systems for improved biomedical research and drug testing. Standardization of microfluidic circuit board connectors is essential to enable reproducible, interoperable, and scalable multi-OoC systems.
method: Development of CAD tools and design methodologies for creating standardized microfluidic circuit board connectors and connection architectures. The work leverages design automation to enable consistent specification and fabrication of connectors across different OoC platforms.
key_novelty: First systematic approach to standardized design of microfluidic circuit board connectors for multi-OoC integration using CAD tools. Addresses the lack of standardization in microfluidic chip interconnection, enabling modular composition of OoC components.
contributions: CAD tool framework for designing standardized microfluidic circuit board connectors
Design standards and specifications for multi-OoC platform connectivity
Methodology for integrating multiple OoC components into unified microfluidic systems
Standardization approach that enables reproducible and interoperable OoC platforms
limitations: Abstract provides limited technical detail on specific design constraints, performance metrics, or validation results. As an invited paper, likely presents a vision and framework rather than comprehensive experimental evaluation.
